text:
I saw two red suns ruling the sky
Topaz lights beaded on their rays
and I stretched out both my hands, hungry for infinity,
to clasp within them an ineffable myth.


The two red pupils, like roses of the sky,
blinded my pupils, proud in their longing
to gaze directly at the diamond glints.


Then, like the crack of knots breaking…
Proud storms threading themselves through the seas;
birth of the gods… A god's groan…
and mouths biting one another in a supreme farewell!


Later, a sonata sweeter than honey;
the agony of lilies in that garden.
a palace of gold and gold where a sorceress dwells
who has slept a hundred years beneath an evil curse.


And then white hands scattering roses
over the hidden, serene soul of things…
And a silence of death, weary and sepulchral,
where the poisonous lotus of evil takes hold.


And then morning arriving at the windows
of the wretched room where I bite my sorrows…
And then another day sketched in the weeping
of my sunless days, of my goldless suns!…

translation.title: The Dream
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the dream's abrupt cinematic sequence—red suns, divine rupture, enchanted palace, deathly silence, and the return to the poor room—along with its surreal repetitions.
